item.title: FDA to hold public hearing on psychedelic drugs as Trump-driven push gathers pace
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration will hold a public hearing on Monday to gather feedback on the potential therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs, the latest step in a months-long push by President Donald Trump's administration to speed up development of the treatments for serious mental illnesses.
item.dc:creator: Puyaan Singh, Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration will hold a public hearing on Monday to gather feedback on the potential therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs, the latest step in a months-long push by President Donald Trump's administration to speed up development of the treatments for serious mental illnesses. The hearing is part of a broader push launched in April, when President Donald Trump ordered the FDA to focus on qualifying psychedelic drug programs for its priority-voucher program. The order also directed the FDA to work with the Drug Enforcement Administration on a pathway for some patients to obtain investigational treatments under the federal Right to Try law, which allows certain seriously ill patients to seek experimental therapies, and to increase collaboration with the Department of Veterans Affairs. Since then, the FDA has issued priority vouchers to three companies developing psychedelic-based treatments, one for psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression, another for psilocybin for major depressive disorder and a third for methylone for post-traumatic stress disorder. The hearing will focus on practical issues that could shape how psychedelic therapies are tested and delivered, including provider training and credentials, patient screening and monitoring, access and reimbursement, clinic capacity and the collection of long-term safety data. The FDA said it is not seeking views on individual drug applications, the scheduling of controlled substances or the legalization of psychedelics. Robert Barrow, CEO of Definium Therapeutics, which is developing an LSD-based therapy, told Reuters that the hearing offers "a nice opportunity for that continuing public dialogue" among regulators, clinicians and patients. He said regulators and industry should treat psychedelics "like it's normal drug development, normal science, normal medicine," rather than as an unusually novel category requiring special treatment. Just days before the hearing, senior FDA officials, including Michael Davis, acting head of the agency's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, published a paper in the New England Journal of Medicine outlining a framework for developing and approving psychedelic drugs and saying the agency was "meeting this moment" on hard-to-treat conditions such as major depressive disorder and PTSD. Jefferies analysts said the framework suggested the FDA was willing to consider flexible trial designs to address challenges including "functional unblinding," when a drug's noticeable psychoactive effects reveal to participants which treatment they received. The agency has indicated that developers could use questionnaires, blinded central raters and, in some studies, lower doses or active comparators, which mimic some peripheral or mild psychological effects, to help address that problem, the analysts said. The administration's support has stirred fresh investor interest in the sector, with industry executives telling Reuters that it could improve coordination between the FDA and the Drug Enforcement Administration and help reduce regulatory delays, even as researchers noted that approved treatments were still likely years away. Continued alignment among regulators, clinicians and developers on a safe, supervised rollout should benefit AtaiBeckley (ATAI.O) , Compass Pathways (CMPS.O) , Definium Therapeutics (DFTX.O) , Helus Pharma and GH Research (GHRS.O) , analysts said.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS L'Europe, sauf Londres, finit dans le rouge, bond du pétrole et des rendements
item.description: Les principales Bourses européennes, hormis Londres, ont terminé dans le rouge lundi et Wall Street était également en baisse à la mi-séance dans un contexte de fortes tensions sur le marché obligataire, d'envolée des cours pétroliers et de mises en garde sur l'intelligence artificielle (IA).
item.dc:creator: Claude Chendjou
item.content:encoded: Les principales Bourses européennes, hormis Londres, ont terminé dans le rouge lundi et Wall Street était également en baisse à la mi-séance dans un contexte de fortes tensions sur le marché obligataire, d'envolée des cours pétroliers et de mises en garde sur l'intelligence artificielle (IA). À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) a fini sur une perte de 0,76% à 8.117,78 points. Le Footsie britannique (.FTSE) a avancé de 0,44%, soutenu par les valeurs liées aux hydrocarbures. Le Dax allemand (.GDAXI) a reflué de 0,60%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) a perdu 1,08%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) 0,50% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) 0,48%. Au moment de la clôture en Europe, le Dow Jones (.DJI) recule de 0,12%, le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) de 0,33% et le Nasdaq (.IXIC) de 0,37%. Ce dernier indice a touché en séance un creux de six semaines, à 25.992 points, les actions liées à l'IA pesant sur le sentiment du marché. Des sociétés américaines comme [USN:L8N4560FD TEXT:"Microsoft"] (MSFT.O) , xAI, [USN:L6N454074 TEXT:"Anthropic"] ou encore OpenAI, ont appelé à un ralentissement du développement de l'IA en raison de craintes liées à la sécurité. Cet appel à la prudence intervient alors que les investisseurs étaient déjà sur la réserve à la veille de la réunion de deux jours de la Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed). La banque centrale américaine pourrait relever mercredi ses taux directeurs de 25 points de base pour juguler une inflation des prix à la consommation ([USN:ZRN00EJFL TEXT:"CPI"]), ressortie vendredi, à 3,4% sur un an en août, contre un objectif à moyen terme de 2% fixé par la Fed. Outre la Fed, la semaine en cours sera marquée par les décisions de la Banque du Japon (BoJ) et de la Banque d'Angleterre (BoE), après celles de la Banque centrale européenne ([USN:L8N4521LV TEXT:"BCE"]), ce qui rend les investisseurs particulièrement nerveux. "Le sentiment d'une hausse des taux se propage aux Etats-Unis", constate Rainer Guntermann, stratégiste taux chez Commerzbank, notant que le président de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, "serait confronté à des problèmes de crédibilité s'il ne mettait pas en pratique ses récentes déclarations restrictives". Sur le [USN:L8N4561AH TEXT:"marché obligataire"], le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à dix ans a dépassé le seuil des 5%, au plus haut depuis octobre 2023, dans un contexte de pressions inflationnistes, d'inquiétudes budgétaires et d'émissions massives de titres de créances, notamment pour financer les dépenses liées à l'intelligence artificielle (IA). VALEURS EN EUROPE Dans un contexte d'inquiétudes sur l'IA, les spécialistes français des puces comme Soitec (SOIT.PA) et STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) ont chuté respectivement de 12,82% et 6,58%, tandis qu'ailleurs en Europe, ASML (ASML.AS) , ASMI (ASMI.AS) , Infineon (IFXGn.DE) ont décroché de 6,24% à 8,26%. Les groupes liés aux centres de données comme Legrand (LEGD.PA) et Schneider (SCHN.PA) ont abandonné respectivement 6,69% et 6,54%. GSK (GSK.L) a gagné 4,74% à la faveur de l'annonce de résultats d'essais cliniques positifs pour deux médicaments contre le cancer du poumon. Le compartiment de la santé (.SXDP) sur le Stoxx 600 a fini sur un gain de 2,72%. Zegona Communications (ZEG.L) s'est adjugé 3,53% en réaction à des informations de médias espagnols d'un possible rachat de Vodafone Espagne par Telefonica (TEF.MC) (+0,57%). CHANGES Le dollar prend 0,42% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) alors que la baromètre Fedwatch de CME Group montre que les marchés évaluent la probabilité d'une hausse des taux de la Fed mercredi à environ 90%, contre 60% la semaine dernière. Le billet vert a touché en séance un sommet depuis le 2 septembre, à 99,648 points. "La situation dans le Golfe reste préoccupante, et des informations liées à l'IA pèsent davantage sur les marchés actions, un contexte dans lequel le dollar devrait rester soutenu", explique Francesco Pesole, stratégiste en devises chez ING. L'euro cède 0,52%, à 1,1539 dollar, après avoir reflué en séance à un plus bas d'un mois, à 1,1524. La livre sterling s'échange à 1,3480 dollar, en baisse de 0,27%, les marchés anticipant que la BoE devrait maintenir sa politique inchangée jeudi, malgré des divergences entre ses membres. TAUX A la clôture des Bourses en Europe, le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à dix ans s'affiche à 4,967%, après un bond en séance à 5,0142%. Celui du Bund allemand de même échéance a fini en hausse de près de trois points de base, à 3,5307%, après avoir progressé de plus de 16 points de base la semaine dernière, soit sa plus forte hausse hebdomadaire depuis la première semaine de mars, juste après le début de la guerre en Iran. Plusieurs responsables de la BCE ont fait part lundi de leurs inquiétudes quant à la hausse des prix de l'énergie, citant non seulement les prix du pétrole, mais aussi ceux du [USN:L6N4560H2 TEXT:"gaz"] et d'autres indicateurs. Les marchés monétaires anticipent au moins une nouvelle hausse des taux de la BCE cette année et n'excluent pas deux autres relèvements d'ici février 2027. L'écart de rendement entre le Bund et l'OAT à dix ans s'est rapproché en séance du seuil psychologique des 100 points de base, à 97,7, alors que l'incertitude demeure sur le projet de budget de la France, dont le texte doit être déposé à l'Assemblée nationale au plus tard le 6 octobre. PÉTROLE Les cours pétroliers ont touché lundi leur plus haut niveau depuis 16 semaines, après que de nouvelles frappes contre des infrastructures énergétiques saoudiennes et des attaques contre des navires au Moyen-Orient, ce qui exacerbe les craintes sur l'approvisionnement énergétique. [USN:L6N4560IP TEXT:"L'Arabie saoudite"] a en outre demandé le report de la réunion qui devait se tenir lundi entre les pays du Golfe et l'Iran pour discuter des moyens de garantir la sécurité de la navigation dans le détroit d'Ormuz Le Brent grimpe de 3,66% à 108,48 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) bondit de 3,73% à 103,81 dollars , après avoir gagné en séance plus de 4%, soit un sommet depuis le 19 mai. A SUIVRE MARDI: [USN:L8N4531CM] LA SITUATION SUR LES MARCHÉS (Certaines données peuvent accuser un léger décalage)

item.title: India bars bank charges on UPI payments up to 2,000 rupees
item.description: India on Monday notified changes in the Payment And Settlement Act, specifying that banks cannot impose charges on payments via Unified Payments Interface transactions of up to 2,000 Indian rupees ($20.93).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India on Monday notified changes in the Payment And Settlement Act, specifying that banks cannot impose charges on payments via Unified Payments Interface transactions of up to 2,000 Indian rupees ($20.93). A government gazette notification specified RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions of up to 2,000 Indian rupees as electronic modes of payment, and said no bank or system provider shall impose any direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving payments through these modes. ($1 = 95.5500 Indian rupees)

item.title: Russian convoy resupplies Syria coastal facilities for first time since Moscow-Damascus deal
item.description: A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country.
item.dc:creator: Feras Dalatey
item.content:encoded: A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country. The operation offers an early indication that Moscow is continuing to resupply facilities at Tartous port and the Hmeimim airbase under [USN:L6N446038 TEXT:"the new deal"], which provides for civilian facilities used by Russia to be transferred to Syrian control and military sites to be turned into joint training centres. Russian forces are [USN:L6N4480K0 TEXT:"to remain"] at the bases under the agreement. Russia has used Hmeimim and Tartous to project power across the Mediterranean, Middle East and Africa. Tartous provides Moscow with its only naval repair and replenishment facility in the Mediterranean. Moscow has supplied both sites in recent months but last week's was the first since the August 9 agreement was announced. The four-vessel convoy arrived at the Mediterranean port of Tartous on September 7, according to movements tracked by Reuters and maritime intelligence firm SynMax. Satellite imagery verified by Reuters showed the Russian Ro-Ro cargo ship Sparta and navy replenishment oiler Akademik Pashin docked on September 8 in Tartous at piers 3 and 4, respectively. A Reuters reporter saw the two vessels docked there on September 9, while Russian tanker General Skobelev remained offshore. A surveillance balloon was seen flying over the port during the unloading operation. A Syrian military source and a Russian-Syrian businessman familiar with the operation said Sparta unloaded supplies including ammunition destined for Hmeimim and Tartous. Reuters could not independently confirm the contents of the shipment or their intended recipients. SynMax identified the fourth vessel in the convoy as Admiral Levchenko, a Russian Udaloy-class destroyer. Syria’s General Authority of Ports and Customs and Russia's embassy in Damascus did not respond to requests for comment. VESSELS SAILED DARK The vessels stopped transmitting their signal shortly after crossing Strait of Gibraltar towards the Mediterranean. Reuters tracked the group via satellite imagery as it continued east and ultimately reached the Syrian coast. Sparta has long been used in Russian military logistics in Syria and is under U.S. sanctions. General Skobelev is also under Western sanctions over transporting Russian oil. Damascus and Moscow reached the agreement over Hmeimim and Tartous after 18 months of negotiations following the December 2024 overthrow of former President Bashar al-Assad, a close Russian ally.

item.title: Canadian dollar hits 12-day low as inflation data meets expectations
item.description: The Canadian dollar weakened to a 12-day low against its U.S. counterpart on Monday and bond yields rose, as domestic inflation data met expectations and after the greenback notched broad-based gains ahead of a Federal Reserve interest rate decision this week.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar weakened to a 12-day low against its U.S. counterpart on Monday and bond yields rose, as domestic inflation data met expectations and after the greenback notched broad-based gains ahead of a Federal Reserve interest rate decision this week. The loonie was trading 0.3% lower at 1.3915 per U.S. dollar, or 71.86 U.S. cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since September 2 at 1.3929. "The driver is clearly a stronger U.S. dollar and that has been encouraged by the shift in expectations on Fed policy," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex LLC. The [USN:L1N4560CJ TEXT:"U.S. dollar"] (.DXY) rose across the board as conflict in the Middle East pushed up [USN:L1N455088 TEXT:"oil prices"] and sent investors towards the safe-haven currency, and as investors bet the Fed would hike on Wednesday for the first time in more than two years. "I think that the U.S.-Canadian trade conflict is a negative as well," said Chandler, adding that investors doubted a [USN:S8N42A05A TEXT:"trade deal"] could come soon as was suggested on Saturday by U.S. President Donald Trump. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomes dozens of global investors to Toronto this week, [USN:L6N4521CS TEXT:"hoping to lure investments"] for more than 160 projects that he says are key to steering Canada's economy through a trade war with the United States. Canada's [USN:L4N4560SD TEXT:"consumer price index"] rose 3% year-over-year in August. That matched the previous month's pace and economists' forecasts but left inflation well above the Bank of Canada's 2% target. BoC Governor Tiff Macklem has said that policymakers were prepared to raise borrowing costs multiple times if inflation remained too high. Canadian bond yields rose across a flatter curve. The 2-year was up 2.7 basis points at 3.384%, after earlier touching its highest level since August 2024 at 3.437%.

item.title: German finance minister lays out demands to UniCredit CEO on possible Commerzbank takeover
item.description: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil laid out demands to UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel in Berlin on Monday over the possible takeover of Commerzbank , the German ministry said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil laid out demands to UniCredit (CRDI.MI) CEO Andrea Orcel in Berlin on Monday over the possible takeover of Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) , the German ministry said in a statement. They included Commerzbank remaining listed on the stock exchange, keeping its base in Frankfurt and continuing to finance German medium-sized companies at home and abroad, the statement said. The meeting marked a turning point in the two-year battle for control of one of Germany's biggest banks after Germany failed in its attempt to stymie a takeover. "In a constructive discussion with Mr. Orcel, I made it clear that the further negotiations must be conducted responsibly," Klingbeil said in a written statement.

item.title: Spanish minister demands justice after violent death of young woman in Mexico
item.description: Spain's Minister of Foreign Affairs demanded justice after the violent death of a Spanish college student in a state neighboring Mexico City, a case that media reports said was a stabbing and local authorities are investigating as a femicide.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain's Minister of Foreign Affairs demanded justice after the violent death of a Spanish college student in a state neighboring Mexico City, a case that media reports said was a stabbing and local authorities are investigating as a femicide. "We want to get to the bottom of this," Foreign Affairs Minister Jose Manuel Albares told reporters during a visit to Andorra. Spanish authorities are in contact with the family of the young woman, who has been identified as Claudia Tacoronte. Mexico has long struggled with high rates of gender-based killings, or femicides. The University of Granada student was on an academic exchange program with the Autonomous University of Morelos State. According to local Mexican media, which cited police sources, 21-year-old Tacoronte died from stab wounds. Tacoronte's body was found late Saturday in the surroundings of the Casa de Cultura in the town of Cuautla, about 100 kilometers from Mexico City. In a statement, the University of Granada said it condemned Tacoronte's "murder", while students and faculty there held a minute of silence. Morelos State Prosecutor Fernando Blumenkron said the death was being investigated as a femicide and pledged to pursue every line of investigation to establish the motives behind the crime and identify the person responsible.

item.title: TotalEnergies, Iraq have agreed to start talks on energy projects, Iraq, France say
item.description: TotalEnergies and the Iraqi government have agreed to start discussions on energy projects in the country, according to a joint French-Iraqi statement on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) and the Iraqi government have agreed to start discussions on energy projects in the country, according to a joint French-Iraqi statement on Monday. The projects would involve large-scale investments and would be aimed at boosting Iraqi oil production while contributing to improving energy sovereignty and the country's energy transition, the statement said.

item.title: US invests in critical minerals but China maintains grip
item.description: Despite U.S. government initiatives, China remains dominant in the supply of critical minerals crucial for clean energy.
item.dc:creator: Anna Flávia Rochas
item.content:encoded: Investment in rare earth refining by the U.S. and Malaysia helped reduce China's supply concentration in this segment from over 90% in 2023 to 85% in 2025, but excluding rare earths, China's average share in critical minerals refining rose from 70% to 72%, data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows. Even if all global planned rare earth refining projects come online as scheduled, China's market share in rare earth refining is only projected to fall to 70%-73% by 2035, IEA said in its Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 report published in July. Graphite, magnet rare earths, Yttrium, and cobalt are among the key minerals most exposed to global supply vulnerabilities, according to the IEA. Magnet rare earths are used in wind turbines, Yttrium is applied in solar converters and capacitors, while graphite, cobalt, manganese and nickel are used in battery energy storage systems. Global demand for critical minerals is forecast to at least double by 2040, largely driven by energy technologies including battery storage, solar and wind, electricity networks and electric vehicles, IEA said. CHART: Share of refined material production by country in 2025 Source: International Energy Agency (2026) The U.S. is pursuing a multipronged strategy to build resilience in critical minerals supply and reduce the dependence on China, providing funding to expand local production, purchasing equity stakes in mining and refining companies, signing framework agreements with international partners and encouraging price floors for minerals. The Trump administration says it has signed or approved 160 critical minerals deals totaling more than $40 billion since January 2025. Government support must be consistent over the long term to encourage investment as projects take time to plan, develop and build, including following through on grant commitment by previous administrations, according to analysts from the Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (C2ES). The Trump administration has cancelled $7.5 billion in clean energy grants approved by the Biden government. It has also sunsetted tax credits for clean energy projects and electric vehicle purchases, impacting the demand-side of the critical mining production chain. Cancellation of previously awarded grants also erode trust in government institutions considered dependable forms of finance, Peter Trousdale, associate Policy Fellow for Regional Programs at C2ES, said. Even with grants in place, they cover only part of the financing needed to build facilities, and demand-side measures such as guaranteed offtake and dependable demand are key to sustaining the supply chain once built. “We need to see [these policies] stay in place for a longer period of time rather than hoping to see really quick results from things like grant announcements or executive orders,” Stephanie Gagnon-Rodriguez, director of Regional Clean Economies at C2ES, told Reuters Events. Join 1,500+ senior decision-makers across energy and finance at Reuters Events Energy LIVE 2026 . Refining and processing remains a bottleneck because it takes time to develop at scale, according to Reed Blakemore, director of Research and Programs for the Global Energy Center of Washington-based think tank Atlantic Council. Strategies that reduce demand for critical materials can play a role, including substitution for different materials, efficiency improvements and product redesign, Blakemore said. "We can't take any options off the table as far as addressing our supply chain security concerns," Blackmore said. US measures To accelerate development, the U.S. government has made equity investments in critical mineral companies including MP Materials, Lithium Americas, USA Rare Earth and others. Another initiative, Project Vault, combines a $10 billion Export-Import Bank (EXIM) loan and nearly $2 billion in private-sector capital to create a critical minerals stockpile. EXIM is also granting loans to develop local critical mineral production, including $25 million to Westwater Resources to support the development of battery-grade natural graphite, in Kellyton, Alabama. The plant will produce U.S. battery-grade coated spherical purified graphite (CSPG) from the adjacent Coosa graphite deposit, used primarily in lithium batteries. Phase one is designed to produce approximately 12,500 metric tons per year of CSPG and commercial operations could start as soon as next year, pending additional funding needed to complete the project, Westwater Resource executives said during the company's earnings call with analysts in August. Download our exclusive report on U.S. grid investment trends. The Department of Energy (DOE) also announced last month $500 million of funding across seven projects to expand critical mineral and material processing for the battery sector. These include a $100 million grant for Lilac Solutions' Great Salt Lake Lithium Project which is expected to double U.S. lithium production capacity by 2028, producing 5,000 tonnes per year of battery-grade lithium carbonate, according to a company statement. A second phase of the project could potentially raise production to 20,000 tonnes per year, enough to support approximately 30 gigawatt-hours of domestic battery manufacturing annually. Short-term risks China's use of export controls for critical minerals illustrates the risk of dependence on foreign suppliers. China introduced export controls on some heavy rare earth elements in April 2025, then amplified restrictions on products containing Chinese rare earths. The country also expanded controls on graphite and high-performance lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material in October 2025, targeting all critical chokepoints in global battery supply chains simultaneously, according to the IEA. China later suspended some of the expanded controls until November 2026 and while it is not expected to reinstate all the export restrictions at once, it is expected to use its dominance in the segment as a lever in negotiations with trading partners, Amit Mathrani, executive director, energy transition at Rabobank, said. As long as uncertainty around China's actions persists, companies will stockpile and accept higher prices, he said. CHART: Annual battery storage additions by region Source: IEA, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence (2026) China currently dominates the global midstream and downstream battery supply chains, particularly in the LFP battery segment. A full implementation of China's export controls would severely restrict the rest of the world's ability to produce batteries in the near term, according to the IEA. Any new restrictions on lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials could impede initiatives underway to develop LFP battery production outside China, the agency said. China processed 70 to 95% of global lithium, cobalt, phosphate, manganese and graphite in 2025 and produced 98% of LFP cathode materials and 80% of global battery cells. Battery action Battery storage developers are already applying risk mitigation strategies to reduce dependence on China's supply chain in order to conform with U.S. federal requirements that forbid supplies from prohibited foreign entities (PFEs) to qualify for tax credits. “Disaggregating your supply chain is a good idea, and then pushing your compliance risk onto your suppliers through warranties or through indemnities, including the replacement parts that you would require in years down the line,” said Mathrani. For exclusive energy insights, sign up to our newsletter . LG Energy Solution, a supplier and developer of battery storage, is working to expand the U.S. production of batteries and diversifying its supply chain, especially for LFP cathode materials. “We’re currently sourcing them stably from our existing suppliers, and at the same time, we’re exploring partnerships with other suppliers with the aim to flexibly respond to local regulations such as non-PFE requirements,” a company spokesperson told Reuters Events. LG Energy Solution's North American production is expected to reach 50 GWh by the end of this year. In August, the company started operations at its new Lansing Battery Plant in Michigan, which will help U.S. customers meet domestic content requirements. The supplier also closed an offtake agreement to source 8,000 tons of U.S.-produced, battery-quality lithium carbonate from Smackover Lithium over 10 years, as part of its commitment to sourcing local production in major markets.

item.title: UK government seeks to acquire insolvent specialist steelmaker
item.description: Britain's government said on Monday it was drawing up a plan to purchase Speciality Steel UK, a manufacturer that has previously supplied the auto, aero and defence industries, and which entered liquidation in August 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's government said on Monday it was drawing up a plan to purchase Speciality Steel UK, a manufacturer that has previously supplied the auto, aero and defence industries, and which entered liquidation in August 2025. Before entering liquidation, Speciality Steel was part of Liberty Steel, owned by commodities tycoon Sanjeev Gupta. The government said it was moving towards public ownership after deciding it could not support a proposed private sector bid for the company, which has sites in northern and central England and supports more than 1,300 jobs. "We do not intervene in private companies lightly. But nor can we simply stand aside and allow the future of this company and over 1,300 jobs to be decided by default," business minister Jonathan Reynolds said. "Working towards public acquisition will keep options open while we work with local leaders, workers, industry and investors to determine the best long-term future for these sites." The government said any purchase was subject to due diligence and would be funded from existing government budgets. It did not set out how much the acquisition could cost.

item.title: Trump afirma que él decidirá si EEUU trabajará para alcanzar un acuerdo con Irán
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump afirmó el lunes que Irán quiere llegar a un acuerdo y que él decidirá si Estados Unidos participará en esos esfuerzos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump afirmó el lunes que Irán quiere llegar a un acuerdo y que él decidirá si Estados Unidos participará en esos esfuerzos. "La nación en decadencia de Irán quiere llegar a un acuerdo, con urgencia y a toda costa. Yo determinaré si Estados Unidos decide participar o no, una posibilidad a la que estamos abiertos", escribió Trump en Truth Social.

item.title: ドイツがEUに対中強硬策働きかけ、PHEV車への関税も模索－関係者
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ドイツは戦略産業を中国から守るため、広範な経済安全保障策を準備している。中国製のプラグインハイブリッド（PHEV）車に対する新たな関税も盛り込まれる可能性がある。

この計画に詳しい関係者によると、ドイツの各省庁は中国に対してどのような弱みがあるかを洗い出し、対抗措置を検討。新たな関税や合弁事業の義務付け、対内・対外投資審査および輸出管理体制の強化などの案が上がっている。

メルツ首相の政権は、10月14日の閣議承認を目指している。そこでの承認を経て、欧州連合（EU）全体で支持を求める意向だという。

この動きは、ドイツが対中政策が強硬路線にかじを切ったことの表れだ。ドイツはこれまで、輸出主導型の経済や中国との深い経済的なつながりを背景に、対中強硬には慎重な姿勢を取ってきた。

だが、EUはいまや1日当たり10億ユーロ（約1780億円）を超える対中貿易赤字を計上。フォルクスワーゲン（VW）はドイツを中心とした世界での従業員削減数を10万人に増やすなど、下り坂にある同国工業では発表済みのものだけで数万人が削減対象となっている。

新たな計画は、ドイツが中国とより相互的な関係を目指しているという具体的な示唆になる。メルツ氏は今年これに先立ち、「われわれは中国の力と経済力を過小評価していた」と述べ、欧州は「重大な戦略的転換点」に直面していると続けた。

関係者によると、ドイツは10月にブリュッセルで開かれるEU首脳会議や、同月下旬に予定される中国との協議を前に、他のEU加盟国の支持を取り付けようとフランスと連携している。両国政府は共同意見書のとりまとめを進めており、これをEU全体の措置を打ち出す土台として他の加盟国と共有する計画だ。

ドイツ経済省の報道官はコメントの要請に応じなかった。それぞれの措置はまだ一つの草案にまとめられておらず、閣内で合意に達する保証もない。

中国企業はバリューチェーンにおける付加価値を急速に向上させ、自動車や機械などの産業で欧州の製造業に挑むようになった。ドイツ連邦統計局によると、2025年のドイツの対中輸出は9.7%減の813億ユーロとなった一方、輸入は8.8%増の1706億ユーロに拡大した。

item.title: Waymo to bring autonomous ride-hailing to Las Vegas
item.description: Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo said on Monday it will offer rides to the general public in Las Vegas, marking its first foray into Nevada, as it expands its robotaxi service in more U.S. states.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) self-driving unit Waymo said on Monday it will offer rides to the general public in Las Vegas, marking its first foray into Nevada, as it expands its robotaxi service in more U.S. states. Waymo, which was valued at $126 billion in February when it raised [USN:L4N3YY1ZH TEXT:"$16 billion"], has been growing its robotaxi fleet as it competes with Amazon's Zoox and Tesla (TSLA.O) in the self-driving vehicle market. Here are more details: Waymo will invite public riders to use its services in Las Vegas as it starts off with a few dozen vehicles, with plans to scale over time. Zoox was the only robotaxi operator in the city offering paid rides to the public after it began commercial operations last month. Las Vegas is Waymo's first public robotaxi market in Nevada, adding to its push beyond its established operations in California, Texas, Florida and Arizona. Earlier this month, Waymo had announced plans to expand in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa. The Las Vegas service uses Waymo's sixth-generation self-driving system in the Ojai, its robotaxi built on a Zeekr vehicle platform.

item.title: ENERGY WATCH: A marathon, not a sprint
item.description: Just when energy markets thought things couldn't get any more complicated, they did.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: Just when energy markets thought things couldn't get any more complicated, they did. The Middle East conflict took another turn in recent days as Iranian-backed Houthi forces [USN:L8N45402S TEXT:"captured"] Yemen's Red Sea coastline, tightening their grip on the Bab el-Mandeb strait, while [USN:L6N453173 TEXT:"drone strikes"] on a key Saudi oil pipeline disrupted supplies equivalent to around [USN:L6N455029 TEXT:"4% of global supply"]. Oil prices responded by climbing by over 3% on Monday to $108 a barrel. Add in the [USN:L8N4550E9 TEXT:"collapse of talks"] between Gulf states on an Iranian-Omani proposal to regulate shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and a sobering picture is emerging: this is no longer a short, sharp energy shock. Markets are increasingly pricing in a prolonged and unpredictable test of global economic resilience. For more on that, [USN:L6N45502N TEXT:"check out my latest column"]. The Iran conflict has become an increasingly awkward political problem for U.S. President Donald Trump ahead of November's midterm elections. During a visit to Ireland on Sunday, which included both business meetings and a round of golf, Trump said he still expected the Iran war to end this year, possibly shortly after the midterms. When it does, he predicted, gasoline prices would "drop like a rock." That may prove optimistic. When the war will end is anyone's guess, but fuel prices look unlikely to collapse anytime soon. The Middle East conflict has severely curtailed global refining capacity, while months of Ukrainian drone attacks have left significant portions of Russia's refining sector damaged. Indeed, Trump also urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to [USN:S8N41C0VK TEXT:"halt strikes"] on Russian diesel infrastructure after U.S. diesel prices surged to a record above $6 a gallon last week. The White House clearly wants to [USN:S8N41C0VY TEXT:"draw a line"] under both the Iran war and the Hormuz standoff. For now, however, Tehran appears to have other ideas. In other news: Silent treatment: Arab states in the Gulf called off a meeting with Iran planned for Monday, while Yemen's Houthis launched a new attack on Saudi Arabia after fighting that has extended the Middle East war to another theatre and [USN:L8N4550E9 TEXT:"further jeopardised global oil supplies"]. Dangote goes public: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday [USN:L8N4530UY TEXT:"launched"] Africa's largest-ever share sale, opening ownership of his giant refinery to retail investors and [USN:L8N4530UY TEXT:"raising funds for further expansion"]. LNG superpower: U.S. liquefied natural gas supply will continue growing and could account for roughly 30% of global LNG output by 2030, [USN:SPN45600P TEXT:"according to an ExxonMobil executive"]. Two-tier oil market: Geopolitical disruptions are creating a huge price gap between crude that can move freely and barrels trapped behind logistical bottlenecks, [USN:L1N45600P TEXT:"explains ROI Asia Commodities Columnist Clyde Russell"]. Rare earth, very rare politics: An obscure member of the rare earths family is going to be high on the agenda when China's President Xi Jinping meets with Trump later this month in Washington. [USN:L8N45121I TEXT:"ROI Metals Columnist Andy Home breaks it down"]. As ever, don't hesitate to contact me at ron.bousso@thomsonreuters.com or follow me on LinkedIn with any questions or thoughts. Subscribe to get Ron Bousso's Power Up newsletter delivered to your inbox every Monday and Thursday. Opinions expressed are those of the author. They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles , is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: What Amodei, Altman and Musk have said about AI risks, stoking 'doom' fears
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called for a slowdown in the pace of advanced AI development, winning rare backing from SpaceXAI's Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and sparking a debate over AI "doomerism".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called for a slowdown in the pace of advanced AI development, winning rare backing from SpaceXAI's Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and sparking a debate over AI "doomerism". [USN:S8N41C0VQ TEXT:"President Donald Trump dismissed the warnings"] about AI's potential risks as exaggerated, as the U.S. races to maintain its lead against China for technological leadership, while Anthropic bumped AI risk assessment to "low" from "very low" last month. The debate has also started at a critical time for Anthropic as it [USN:L6N45316U TEXT:"prepares for a potential IPO"] and after OpenAI pushed back its own listing plans. Here is what some AI leaders have said about risks associated with the technology : DARIO AMODEI, CEO OF ANTHROPIC In an essay titled " We Must Pace the Frontier ", Amodei said AI progress has accelerated "drastically faster" since summer 2026, driven primarily by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI. He cited the [USN:L6N43V159 TEXT:"OpenAI-Hugging Face incident"], where an AI "swarm" conducted cybersecurity attacks, as a pivotal event demonstrating AI's potential for "catastrophic damage" if capabilities grow without guardrails. Amodei proposed a "three-step plan" for pacing AI development, including stronger safety testing and independent evaluations of advanced AI models, coordination among leading AI companies and greater international cooperation. SAM ALTMAN, CEO OF OPENAI "I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier. This has been a primary topic of discussions we've had at OpenAI in recent weeks," Altman said as he reposted Amodei's post on X . Altman said OpenAI has the intention to adopt the idea proposed by Anthropic by committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access. Altman was warning about the risks well before the current AI boom. In a 2015 essay titled " Machine Intelligence, part 1 ", he said the "development of superhuman machine intelligence is probably the greatest threat to the continued existence of humanity". ELON MUSK, CEO OF SPACEX "Dario is right," the billionaire entrepreneur said on X , responding to Amodei's post. Musk was among backers of a 2023 push by the non-profit Future of Life Institute to halt AI development for six months to allow time for safety guardrails. He was also among a group of AI and robotics researchers who wrote an open letter in 2015 that advocated a global ban on "offensive autonomous weapons", arguing against making "new tools for killing people."

item.title: Dólar se dispara y va camino a su mejor jornada desde junio antes de la decisión de la Fed
item.description: El dólar se encamina a su mejor jornada desde junio, mientras los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años superan el 5% y los mercados se preparan para la decisión de tasas de la Reserva Federal del miércoles.
item.dc:creator: George Lei
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — El dólar se apreció este lunes y va camino de registrar su mejor jornada desde el 17 de junio, fecha en la que tuvo lugar la primera reunión del FOMC bajo la presidencia de Kevin Warsh. El índice Bloomberg Dollar Spot subió hasta un 0,6%, tras mantenerse sin cambios el viernes a pesar de un aumento superior al esperado en un indicador de inflación subyacente. Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años subieron ligeramente por quinta sesión consecutiva este lunes hasta superar el 5%, su nivel más alto desde 2023. Por su parte, el crudo WTI se mantuvo por encima de los US$100 por barril tras alcanzar su nivel intradía más alto desde el 19 de mayo. Ver más: Dólares físicos, digitales o stablecoins: usos, diferencias y desventajas El dólar ha registrado un rendimiento inferior al esperado en estas últimas dos semanas, a pesar de que los elevados precios de la energía, los datos de inflación y empleo de agosto, así como el mensaje halcón de Warsh en Jackson Hole, “deberían haberlo impulsado al alza”, afirmó Meera Chandan, codirectora de estrategia cambiaria global de JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ). “Por el momento, nos mantenemos fieles a nuestra postura alcista respecto al dólar estadounidense previa a la reunión del FOMC, centrándonos específicamente en las divisas con bajos rendimientos, como la corona sueca y el dólar canadiense”. Todas las divisas del G-10 retrocedieron el lunes, con el dólar neozelandés y la corona sueca a la cabeza. Ambas están en camino de caer un 1% en la jornada. El yen japonés bajó más de un 0,8%, su peor resultado en una semana. Por su parte, los mercados de opciones también se están preparando para una mayor fortaleza del dólar en el futuro. Las reversiones de riesgo a un mes del índice del dólar volvieron a situarse en territorio positivo por primera vez desde el 2 de septiembre, una señal de que los operadores se están posicionando para obtener más ganancias. Ver más: ¿Precio del dólar más fuerte? Tabla de las nuevas proyecciones para las monedas de Latinoamérica en 2027 No obstante, persisten las dudas sobre hasta dónde puede llegar el repunte actual. “Existe un riesgo asimétrico para el dólar, con ganancias limitadas derivadas de una postura restrictiva de la Fed, ya que los mercados ya están descontando unos 100 puntos básicos de endurecimiento en los próximos 12 meses”, afirmó Elias Haddad, director global de estrategia de mercados de Brown Brothers Harriman & Co. La decisión de la Reserva Federal sobre las tasas de interés está prevista para el miércoles. “Por su parte, una sorpresa moderada conllevaría mayores riesgos a la baja”, añadió Haddad. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: ロシア・ウクライナ、エネルギー施設への攻撃停止で合意－トランプ氏
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領は、ウクライナとロシアが互いのエネルギー施設を攻撃しないことで合意したと明らかにした。製油所への攻撃でディーゼル価格が過去最高水準まで上昇するなかでの発言だ。
「ウクライナはロシアのエネルギー施設を攻撃しないことに合意した。ロシアも同じように合意した！」と、トランプ氏はSNSに投稿。ディーゼル価格の急騰は、イランでの戦争ではなく、こうした攻撃が原因だとの見方を示した。
ロシアとウクライナは、こうした合意に達したかどうかを公式には明らかにしていない。エネルギー施設への攻撃停止を巡っては、これまでも停戦の仲介が試みられたが、実現しなかった。
原題：Trump Says Ukraine, Russia Agree Not to Hit Energy

item.title: Oil stocks in US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fall to lowest level since 1982
item.description: Stocks of crude oil in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 285 million barrels last week, the lowest level since November 1982, according to data from the Department of Energy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Stocks of crude oil in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 285 million barrels last week, the lowest level since November 1982, according to data from the Department of Energy. The drawdowns are part of a U.S. agreement to release 172 million barrels from the facility.

item.title: Los grandes se recuperan, dice Wolff sobre Russell tras GP de España de la F1
item.description: El jefe de Mercedes, Toto Wolff, aseguró a George Russell que contará con todo el apoyo del equipo para dar rienda suelta a su talento y luchar por los campeonatos de Fórmula 1, a pesar de haber quedado eclipsado esta temporada por su compañero de equipo Kimi Antonelli, de 20 años.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: El jefe de Mercedes, Toto Wolff, aseguró a George Russell que contará con todo el apoyo del equipo para dar rienda suelta a su talento y luchar por los campeonatos de Fórmula 1, a pesar de haber quedado eclipsado esta temporada por su compañero de equipo Kimi Antonelli, de 20 años. Russell, de 28 años, comenzó la temporada como favorito al título, pero solo ha ganado dos veces frente a las ocho del italiano en las 14 pruebas disputadas hasta la fecha. Segundo en el campeonato, el británico terminó quinto el domingo, mientras que Antonelli celebró la victoria en el primer Gran Premio de España celebrado en el nuevo circuito de Madrid y se colocó con una ventaja de 81 puntos en la clasificación. "En lo que respecta a George, puede haber carreras buenas y carreras malas. Años buenos y años malos. Pero estamos hablando del piloto que ha ganado todo lo que se podía ganar antes", dijo Wolff a periodistas en Madrid. "Todos y cada uno de los campeonatos de karting, la Fórmula 3 en su año de debut, la Fórmula 2 en su año de debut… (él) entró en el equipo Williams. Quiero decir, estamos hablando de un piloto de primer nivel". "Tenemos que averiguar qué necesita para poder dar rienda suelta a ese potencial. Y, por supuesto, está el aspecto psicológico", continuó el austriaco. "Si tienes una temporada como la suya este año, te llevas un buen golpe, pero los grandes se recuperan y creo que George tiene todo lo necesario para luchar por los campeonatos". Russell dijo el domingo que, siendo realistas, ya no estaba en la lucha por el título y que solo se centraba en conseguir buenos resultados en las carreras restantes. Es poco habitual que un piloto gane ocho carreras en una temporada y no se lleve el título, pero ya ha ocurrido antes, y a veces el piloto con más victorias no es el campeón. Wolff advirtió que bastarían dos resultados nulos por parte de Antonelli para que Russell volviera a estar en la lucha. Dicho esto, también respaldó a Antonelli para que mantuviera la concentración y no diera nada por sentado. "Kimi, por su personalidad —es muy sensato, un piloto al 100%, no se distrae con nada ajeno a las carreras y tiene una situación familiar estupenda—. Y por eso no veo ningún riesgo de que pierda el norte por ser tan dominante", afirmó el austriaco. "Te aseguro que no está pensando en ello (el título). Por la forma en que este chico es capaz de separar las cosas —ser un chico joven y, al subirse al coche, convertirse en un piloto maduro—, si se dice a sí mismo 'no estoy pensando en el campeonato', es que no está pensando en el campeonato".

item.title: トランプ氏、ロシア・ウクライナがエネ施設攻撃停止で合意と主張
